summary: Interpreted the receipt that carries the double-application discriminator (CheckRun 84f1db1b39974263b5c2222bb4053ce5: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 21 parsed observations, 0 parse errors). Indices 17-19 show the three rejections with the new operands: node 3 seed 35 step 22 and node 1 step 23 both with applied_before=3, applying_before=3, entry_index=4, entry_term=2, one change, joint-entering, joint_now=true and reapplied_entry=false; node 4 step 31 with applied_before=0 and applying_before=0 for the same entry and reapplied_entry=false, i.e. a node rebuilt from persisted state consuming its log from the beginning. Index 20 reports three rejections among 245 configuration changes, 446 restarts, 481 elections, 51 unapplied-change check points, stalled_states=0 and violations=0. Two readings are now settled: the harness did not re-present an entry whose index was already covered by the apply pointer - for nodes 3 and 1 the batch started exactly at applied_before+1 - so the double-application/off-by-one artifact is refuted with a receipt; and the rejections did not come from application lag either, since all three nodes were current with their commit index when the Changer rejected. One reading stays open, which is why the defect claim remains unresolved rather than asserted: the receipt does not show whether the log the node consumed in order legitimately contained a joint-entering change at that position. Since the guard rewrites a joint change when the proposing leader's own configuration is joint or has an unapplied change, two joint-entering changes without an intervening leave would mean one rewrite did not happen - either the guard's premises did not hold at the proposer, or the proposer was not the node that saw the joint state - and that distinction is not decidable from these indices. What the receipt does support is that a node applying its own committed log in order can be handed a change its Changer rejects, with the target's only reaction being the contract's panic: an availability consequence, with no safety violation observed. Counterevidence and limits recorded: violations=0 alongside; all three from one seed and one log position; the lag story is weakened but not fully excluded because the harness can still make a node's configuration lag the leader's while its applied index equals its commit index; the receipt lacks the entry types before index 4 and any leave entry in that log; no rejection was observed at a leader; and only the first three occurrences emit operands.
